limitations: Compliance with screening was only 58.2 percent
The higher crude incidence in the screened arm points to over-diagnosis, which the authors acknowledge
The authors estimate a lead time of about 0.5 years
critique: Allocation was by cluster, with whole factories, schools and enterprises assigned together, but the analysis treated individuals as independent observations; an independent reanalysis calculated that the mortality difference would almost certainly have been non-significant had the clustering been accounted for

384 of the 9,757 people allocated to screening were removed after randomisation because they refused, so the analysis is not intention to treat despite the paper's claim, and every exclusion is on the intervention side

Only HCC deaths were counted and all-cause mortality was never reported, so neither harm from screening and the surgery it leads to nor misattribution of cause of death can be excluded, and the standard safeguard against disease-specific mortality bias is absent

The screened arm's crude incidence was 37 percent higher than the control arm's, which is the signature of over-diagnosis, and the paper offers no analysis of how much of the mortality difference that could generate

Survival comparisons between the arms are timed from diagnosis, which is lead-time biased by construction, and the authors' own estimated lead time of about half a year is of the same order as the survival differences reported

The population is hepatitis B carriers and people with past hepatitis aged 35 to 59 in Shanghai, mostly without documented cirrhosis and screened with alpha-fetoprotein as a co-test, so it maps poorly onto a Western cirrhotic ultrasound surveillance cohort in whom alpha-fetoprotein is no longer recommended as a screening test
Treatment of screen-detected cancers was resection in a pre-BCLC era with no transplantation or ablation pathway, so the mortality benefit depends on a treatment algorithm that no longer exists

The paper's own figures disagree: the narrative gives the stage III split as 22 (25.6 percent) against 45 (62.9 percent) while the table gives 22 against 42 (62.7 percent), and resection in controls is 5 (7.5 percent) in the table against 7.8 percent in the text
Compliance of 58.2 percent means that the measured effect is that of offering screening to a workplace population, and the paper presents no per-protocol or compliance-adjusted estimate alongside it
15042359.n: 18,816 people aged 35 to 59 with serological evidence of hepatitis B infection or a history of chronic hepatitis, recruited from more than 300 factories, enterprises and schools in urban Shanghai between January 1993 and December 1995 and cluster-allocated to 6-monthly alpha-fetoprotein and ultrasound screening (9,757 allocated, 9,373 analysed) or no screening (9,443); cirrhosis was neither required nor excluded
15042359.bottom_line: The single randomised trial behind the recommendation for 6-monthly HCC surveillance, reporting a 37 percent reduction in HCC mortality with screening (83.2 against 131.5 per 100,000). Allocation was by cluster but the analysis treated individuals as independent, 384 people who refused were removed from the screening arm after allocation, and all-cause mortality was never reported.
15042359.funding: No funding statement; the trial predates registries and has no registration number

limitations: Post-randomisation exclusion occurred in 19 of 90 patients assigned to ablation, all of whom withdrew consent and chose resection; the authors state they do not think this affected the results
Mean follow-up was only just beyond 2 years, and the authors state they do not expect a difference with longer follow-up
The sample size was relatively small, and the authors argue a larger sample would not have changed the result because the curves were almost identical
The authors concede that for ablation to work the first session must be followed by CT at 4 weeks and a further session of ablation or ethanol injection if viable tumour remains
critique: The analysis labelled intention to treat is not one: the 90-patient ablation arm includes the 19 patients who actually underwent resection, so 21 percent of the experimental arm received the comparator operation, and the abstract instead quotes the post-randomisation-exclusion analysis of 71 against 90

All 19 consent withdrawals went in the same direction, from ablation to surgery, which is the signature of unconcealed allocation; randomisation is described only as computer-generated numbers in a central registry with no concealment mechanism, no blinding and no independent outcome adjudication

No hazard ratio, confidence interval or p value is printed anywhere for the primary survival comparison; survival was computed by the life-table method and compared by Mantel-Cox, and the result is reported only as the assertion that no difference was found

The multivariable Cox model in Table 2 prints regression coefficients without their signs and no hazard ratios or confidence intervals, and reports serum albumin as the only predictor of survival (p = 0.0018) in a model of nine variables fitted to a cohort with roughly 50 deaths

Four-year survival is the longest estimate reported although mean follow-up was 27.9 and 29.2 months, and no at-risk numbers appear under any of the ten survival curves, so the terminal estimates rest on an unstated handful of patients

The morbidity comparison sets 50 of 90 resections against 3 of 71 ablations, mixing the two different analysis populations in one sentence, and 46 of the 50 surgical events are moderate-to-severe ascites (27) or jaundice beyond 30 days (19) counted as major complications with no validated grading system

The ablation arm's harms were captured only as skin burns (3) and fever (8), with no systematic ascertainment of ascites, jaundice or liver dysfunction at all, which is why its complication count is 3; the two arms were not monitored for the same events

Ablation as tested is a strategy rather than a procedure: complete necrosis was 62.0 percent after the first session and reached 91.5 percent only after repeat ablation or ethanol injection in 21 patients and chemoembolisation in 2, so 8.5 percent of the arm never achieved necrosis yet remained in its survival curve

A single device was used (RF 2000 with a 3.5 cm LeVeen expandable electrode) with the endpoint of a hyperechoic cloud larger than the tumour on ultrasound and no margin requirement, which is not an adequate technique for tumours approaching 5 cm, and 34 of 71 ablated tumours measured 3.1 to 5 cm

Diagnosis was imaging-based with an alpha-fetoprotein threshold: one resected specimen proved to be focal nodular hyperplasia and two patients had disseminated disease found at laparotomy, so at least 3 of 90 surgical patients did not have the disease under study and equivalent misclassification in the ablation arm could not be detected

The stated sample size calculation specifies an alpha risk of 0.05 and a beta risk of 0.8, which is the power rather than the beta risk, and the trial was powered on 2-year recurrence rather than on survival, so the survival conclusion that the paper advertises was never the question the design could answer
The 3 cm and 3.1 to 5 cm subgroup analyses involve 37 and 34 ablation patients and are reported as non-significant with no estimates, confidence intervals or interaction tests given

The comparator is open surgery as practised in one Chinese centre in 1999 to 2004, with a right subcostal incision, routine Pringle manoeuvre in 10 and 5 minute cycles and a mean 19.7-day hospital stay against 9.2 days, so the length-of-stay and analgesia advantages do not transfer to a laparoscopic era

The authors answer each of their three stated limitations by assuming the null they are defending, arguing in turn that the exclusions, the short follow-up and the small sample would not have changed a result whose curves were already superimposed
16495695.n: 180 patients with a solitary HCC of 5 cm or less randomised at one Guangzhou centre between November 1999 and June 2004, drawn from 3,775 patients with HCC hospitalised there; 90 to percutaneous ablation (of whom only 71 received it) and 90 to resection
16495695.bottom_line: The first randomised comparison of percutaneous ablation with resection for a solitary HCC of 5 cm or less, reporting 4-year overall survival of 67.9 versus 64.0 percent and disease-free survival of 46.4 versus 51.6 percent with no significant difference. Nineteen of 90 patients assigned to ablation withdrew and had surgery instead, ablation as delivered needed repeat sessions to reach 91.5 percent necrosis from 62.0 percent after one treatment, and no hazard ratio or confidence interval for the primary comparison appears anywhere in the paper.
16495695.funding: Supported by a grant from the Sciences and Technology Committee of Guangdong Province, China, 2002; no conflict-of-interest statement appears in the article

limitations: The comparison with surgery is historical, drawn from three surgical series, and the authors acknowledge the well-known limitations of historical comparison
Fourteen of 232 eligible patients (6.0 percent) could not be treated because the tumour was poorly visible on ultrasound or lay next to bowel or main bile ducts
Three of the treatment failures occurred next to a large vessel, which the authors attribute to heat loss in the ablation zone
The authors state that a randomised trial of ablation against resection below 2 cm would need a very large sample and is probably not feasible

The authors concede that the high overall recurrence rate shows it is the natural history of the cirrhotic liver, not the first treatment, that governs prognosis, and that all published survival curves reflect repeated multimodal treatment
critique: The 68 percent 5-year survival in the abstract and conclusion is that of the 100 patients retrospectively judged operable; the whole cohort's figure of 55 percent appears only once in the Results and never in the abstract, so the number set against surgical series is a selected subgroup

Operability was assigned by the authors from age 75 or under, alanine transferase under three times normal, bilirubin under 1.5 and absence of portal hypertension, with no surgeon assessing any patient, and operability was not an independent predictor of survival once adjusted (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.31 to 1.26, p = 0.192), so the subgroup that carries the headline does not survive multivariable analysis

Three different complete-response figures appear in the same paper: 216 of 218 (97.2 percent) in the abstract, 214 of 218 (98.1 percent) complete radiological necrosis in the Results and 212 of 218 (97.2 percent) sustained complete local response; 216 of 218 is 99.1 percent, so the abstract's numerator and percentage do not correspond

The classification boundary creates the result: enhancement within the ablation zone or up to 2.0 cm from its border is local recurrence, anything beyond 2.0 cm is a new lesion, which yields a 0.9 percent local recurrence rate in a cohort where 80 percent of patients recurred somewhere in the liver

Disease-free survival of 26 percent at 3 years and 20 percent at 5 years is computed on 82 patients rather than 218, and the paper never states which 82 or why, while quoting confidence intervals as wide as 7 to 36 percent

The 14 patients excluded for poor ultrasound visibility or a high-risk location are precisely the tumours in which ablation fails and resection is straightforward, so the local-control endpoint is measured on ground selected to favour the technique; the paper also states that 218 of 232 is 93.3 percent when it is 94.0 percent

Technique was not standardised in any respect: five departments used at least four different electrode systems, including a 1.5 cm laterally deployed spiral, with power and exposure left to manufacturer recommendation and operator preference, and adequacy was judged by the extent of a hyperechoic cloud rather than by a measured margin on post-treatment imaging

Pathological confirmation of the 97.2 percent local response consists of the explants of the 3 patients who were transplanted and censored at transplantation, so 215 of 218 local responses rest on contrast CT alone, with follow-up imaging only every 4 to 6 months

Patients with any prospect of transplantation were excluded by design, so the cohort systematically omits the patients in whom the choice between ablation and resection carries the greatest consequence, and the authors justify this by Italian organ scarcity rather than by the clinical question

The only significant multivariable predictor of survival is the appearance of new lesions during follow-up (HR 1.97, 1.13 to 3.5), a post-treatment event entered as a predictor of a survival time it partly determines, and alpha-fetoprotein could not be analysed at all because only 11 patients had raised values, so the model contains no measure of tumour biology
Median follow-up was 31 months against 3- and 5-year endpoints in a cohort followed from 6 to 134 months, and no at-risk numbers appear under any survival curve

The surgical mortality the paper contrasts with its own 0 percent is a literature mean of 5 percent spanning 0 to 15 percent across series from different decades and countries, while the Italian hepatitis C surveillance population here (83.9 percent HCV, mean age 68, 44 percent female, 21.5 percent over 75) is compared with Japanese surgical cohorts

One of the four major complications is hyperbilirubinaemia lasting a month, and one is neoplastic seeding, so the 1.8 percent figure that anchors the safety argument contains a tumour implant from the procedure itself

The paper concludes that ablation should be the treatment of choice even when resection is possible, a statement of superiority drawn from an uncontrolled cohort by authors who in the same Discussion declare the controlled test of it unfeasible
18008357.n: 218 of 232 eligible patients with a single HCC of 2.0 cm or less and Child-Pugh A cirrhosis, treated by percutaneous radiofrequency ablation at 5 Italian departments between October 1995 and June 2006; 100 were retrospectively judged potentially operable
18008357.bottom_line: A multicentre cohort showing that radiofrequency ablation of a single HCC of 2 cm or less achieves sustained complete local response in 97.2 percent with no mortality and a 1.8 percent major complication rate. The 68 percent 5-year survival used to argue that ablation can replace resection belongs to a retrospectively defined operable subgroup of 100 patients, not to the cohort, whose 5-year survival was 55 percent with 80 percent recurrence and 20 percent disease-free survival; there is no control group and the authors argue the randomised trial that would settle it is not feasible.
18008357.funding: No funding statement appears; the authors declare no potential conflict of interest

limitations: The number of patients required to show superiority was underestimated because conventional chemoembolisation achieved a 44 percent response rate against the assumed 35 percent, which the authors state
Robust time-to-progression and survival data would require further randomised trials with longer follow-up, as the authors acknowledge
The authors note that conventional chemoembolisation varies widely between centres in drugs, embolic agents, doses and schedules, and that evidence of a survival benefit at 3 years is low
critique: The two arms did not receive comparable drug: the bead arm had a fixed 150 mg of doxorubicin with no adjustment for bilirubin or body surface area while the control arm had 50 to 75 mg per square metre adjusted for both, so roughly double the dose was delivered in the experimental arm and any difference in response or in hepatic enzyme change is confounded with dose rather than with the delivery platform

The primary analysis population is a modified intention-to-treat set restricted to patients who received at least one chemoembolisation, and the attrition was asymmetric (9 of 102 bead patients never treated against 2 of 110 controls), so 11 randomised patients were removed from the comparison in the direction that favours the experimental arm

The adaptive three-stage group sequential design set the final significance boundary at a p value of 0.024 rather than 0.05, and the trial enrolled 212 patients against a design built around 200, so the failed primary endpoint was judged against a boundary the paper does not discuss when describing the result as favourable

Every analysis other than the failed primary endpoint and the primary safety endpoint is described in the Methods as supportive in nature and analysed descriptively, so all the positive statements in the paper are descriptive

The subgroup of more advanced patients (Child-Pugh B, ECOG 1, bilobar or recurrent disease) is described in the Methods as preplanned and in the Results and Discussion as post hoc and hypothesis-generating, with p values unadjusted for multiplicity; this subgroup is the basis for the paper's conclusion that the device offers benefit in more advanced disease

Thirteen patients with bilobar disease received a second embolisation of the other lobe within three weeks as procedure 1B, unevenly distributed (8 bead against 5 control), so treatment intensity differed between arms outside the randomised comparison

The primary endpoint is EASL radiological response at 6 months, a surrogate with no established relation to survival in this setting, and follow-up stopped at 6 months, so the trial cannot answer whether the device changes any outcome a patient would notice

Thirteen patients were downstaged to curative treatment and discontinued (5 bead, 8 control), and 67 of 201 treated patients discontinued treatment altogether, with no accounting for how these departures affect a 6-month response endpoint

The control arm's embolic agent was left to investigator choice while the experimental arm used a single standardised device, so the comparison is between a defined product and a heterogeneous practice
The trial was sponsored by the manufacturer of the device under test, and the paper offers no statement about who performed the analysis or who drafted the manuscript

The later independently conducted PRECISION Italia randomised trial, with no industry sponsor, found no difference in response, time to progression (9 months in both arms) or 2-year survival (56.8 against 55.4 percent, p = 0.949) and was stopped for futility
19908093.n: 212 patients with Child-Pugh A or B cirrhosis and large or multinodular unresectable N0 M0 HCC randomised at European centres to drug-eluting bead chemoembolisation (102) or conventional chemoembolisation (110); the modified intention-to-treat population analysed was 93 and 108 patients who received at least one treatment
19908093.bottom_line: PRECISION V is the trial routinely cited as establishing drug-eluting beads, and it failed its primary endpoint: EASL objective response at 6 months did not differ significantly from conventional chemoembolisation. It is a phase 2 study with a six-month radiological endpoint, no time-to-progression or survival data, a fixed 150 mg doxorubicin dose in the experimental arm against a body-surface-area and bilirubin-adjusted dose in the control arm, and manufacturer sponsorship.
19908093.funding: Sponsored by Biocompatibles UK Ltd, the manufacturer of the DC Bead device under test, as declared in the acknowledgments

limitations: Enrolment was stopped for futility on the recommendation of an external review committee after the second interim analysis, at 177 of 214 planned patients

The power calculation assumed a 40 percent 2-year survival with conventional chemoembolisation and a 20 percentage point absolute gain with beads, which the authors concede was an optimistic view based on the device's theoretical advantages
The pragmatic design permitted referring physicians to use ablation, resection, sorafenib or transplantation after two chemoembolisations, and 36 of 177 patients received further treatment
The authors note the inclusion of BCLC C patients in whom chemoembolisation is debatable
Response was judged by EASL criteria until 2010 and modified RECIST thereafter, mostly on multidetector CT, which the authors accept masks residual tumour after lipiodol
critique: At one month the control arm achieved a significantly higher overall complete response than the beads (59.8 against 43.8 percent, p = 0.036), and the authors explain this as a spurious effect of lipiodol masking, which concedes that the response endpoint in a lipiodol-based comparison is uninterpretable in either direction

The post hoc subgroup analyses point the same way, with conventional chemoembolisation achieving significantly more complete responses in ECOG 0 (p = 0.014) and BCLC A patients (p = 0.027), findings the paper reports without reconciling them against the trend it prefers at 6 months

Survival of patients who became transplantable after downstaging was censored at the day before surgery, so the most successful outcomes in both arms were removed from the survival comparison the trial was powered on

Fewer than a third of patients had unambiguously intermediate-stage disease: 46.3 percent were BCLC A, 26.0 percent were classed BCLC C solely on an ECOG score of 1, and the median largest tumour was 2.6 cm, so the trial did not test beads where their larger drug payload is argued to matter
The reported median survival of 28 and 29 months is explicitly a projection from the 1- and 2-year rates rather than an observed median, since follow-up was a minimum of 2 years

The severe adverse event rate of 6.2 percent with a superselective technique is far below that of the manufacturer-sponsored trial it contradicts, so the absence of a safety advantage for beads may reflect an unusually good conventional technique rather than equivalence of the two devices

Twenty percent of patients received an additional non-randomised treatment after two chemoembolisations, which dilutes the comparison in a trial whose primary endpoint is time to progression and whose power was already compromised

Both arms also differed in the drug delivered (mean 47.2 mg of epirubicin with lipiodol against 57.8 mg of doxorubicin on beads), so the comparison is of two regimens rather than of two delivery systems
Response was assessed on CT at a time when the authors themselves say CT after lipiodol is inadequate, with the choice justified on grounds of availability rather than accuracy

The trial's conclusion that routine use of beads is hard to justify rests on a cost argument of at least 600 euros per treatment rather than on the trial's own data, which cannot exclude a clinically modest difference
24937669.n: 177 of a planned 214 patients with HCC randomised at five Italian centres to conventional chemoembolisation (88) or drug-eluting bead chemoembolisation (89), with a median of two procedures per arm; 46.3 percent were BCLC A, 26.0 percent BCLC C on ECOG 1 alone, and the median largest tumour was 2.6 cm
24937669.bottom_line: PRECISION Italia is the independent test of drug-eluting beads and it was stopped for futility: median time to progression was 9 months in both arms, 2-year survival 56.8 against 55.4 percent (p = 0.949), with less post-procedural pain the only advantage of beads. It cannot establish equivalence, because it was powered for an implausible 20-point survival gain and stopped at 83 percent of its planned size, and nearly half its patients were early-stage with a median tumour under 3 cm.
24937669.funding: No funding source is identified in the article; the authors declare no conflict of interest

limitations: The analysis pools observational and mostly retrospective data, which the authors state limits the ability to control for confounding
Because most included studies did not adjust for known confounders, the authors were forced to use crude measures of association
Four of the eleven studies scored 10 on the QUIPS tool and were rated high risk of bias
The definition of clinical decompensation varied across studies, although all included jaundice and ascites

The authors acknowledge that surgical practice has moved on since the included cohorts, naming laparoscopic resection, reduced clamping and portal vein embolisation, though they argue resection does not lower portal pressure

The authors note that the reliability of observational methodology is hard to judge from published reports, which is why they restricted the search to full publications and excluded the grey literature
critique: The search window opens in January 1996 because that is when the authors' own first paper on the question appeared, and four of the eleven included studies come from the authors' own group, so a meta-analysis described in its Discussion as validating the EASL and AASLD recommendations is conducted by the authors of those recommendations using their own data

The decompensation subgroup estimate that drives the recommendation to measure the hepatic venous pressure gradient (pooled OR 14.59, 95% CI 2.81 to 80.06) rests on three studies of 29, 40 and 46 patients, two of them from the authors' unit, and the smallest of the three has perfect separation so its true odds ratio is unbounded

The corresponding mortality subgroup estimate for gradient-based studies (OR 8.00, 95% CI 2.59 to 24.69) comes from the same group's 1996 and 1999 papers, so the claim that invasive measurement outperforms surrogates is a comparison between the authors' small prospective series and other groups' larger retrospective ones

That comparison is made between subgroups of studies rather than within patients: no included study measured the gradient and the surrogate criteria in the same patients and compared their prognostic performance, so the conclusion that surrogates cannot exclude clinically significant portal hypertension is not something the pooled data can establish

Only 2 of the 8 survival studies reported portal hypertension as an independent predictor on multivariable analysis, a fact placed in a supplementary table while the abstract and conclusions report the pooled crude odds ratio, so the headline estimate cannot distinguish the harm of operating from the natural history of more advanced cirrhosis

Operative mortality did not differ by portal hypertension status in any study that reported it (11.1 versus 5.1 percent, 4.6 versus 1.1 percent, 0.5 versus 0 percent, all non-significant), so whatever the pooled survival difference represents, it is not perioperative death

Patients with portal hypertension systematically received different operations: anatomical resection in 39 versus 68 percent in the largest study (p < 0.001), 12.1 versus 33.1 percent in another (p = 0.0003), 15.0 versus 31.1 percent in a third (p = 0.001), with less transfusion, so the exposure is confounded with the extent of surgery, and the stratified analysis the authors say addresses this is reported only as data not shown

Several of the sensitivity analyses that support the robustness claim, including the QUIPS low-versus-moderate-to-high comparison and the anatomic-resection strata, are reported as data not shown and cannot be checked

Four different constructs are pooled as one exposure: a gradient of 10 mmHg or more, portal vein pressure of 20 cmH2O or more, the presence of gastro-oesophageal varices, and platelets below 100,000 with a spleen above 12 cm; the prevalence of the resulting exposure ranges from 21.7 to 51.7 percent across studies
No funnel plot, Egger test or any formal assessment of small-study or publication bias is presented, in an analysis whose most extreme subgroup estimates come from its smallest studies

The search covered MEDLINE only, in English only, with no grey literature, no registries and no non-English reports; four full texts could not be obtained and were excluded; only 2 of 11 studies are Asian, and the principal dissenting Asian study was eligible for the survival analysis alone

The one study showing no effect of portal hypertension on 3- or 5-year mortality is the only multicentre study in the set, and the paper offers no examination of why the largest and least selected cohort is the discordant one

Two of the included studies come from the same unit over overlapping years (1989 to 1997 and 1991 to 1994), and the stated rule against duplicate cohorts is satisfied by entering one into the survival pool and the other into the decompensation pool, which conceals rather than removes the overlap

The senior author declares consultancy and grants from Bayer and relationships with nine other companies, and the practical consequence of the recommendation is to move patients with portal hypertension from resection to transplantation, ablation or chemoembolisation, the last of which the Discussion endorses by citing the group's own drug-eluting-bead series
25212123.n: 11 studies with 1,737 patients with cirrhosis and HCC treated surgically; 1,572 patients (574 with and 998 without clinically significant portal hypertension) in the survival analysis with 491 deaths at 3 years and 694 at 5 years, and 1,108 patients (386 with and 722 without) with 197 decompensation events
25212123.bottom_line: Pools 11 observational studies and finds that clinically significant portal hypertension roughly doubles 3- and 5-year mortality after resection for HCC (pooled OR 2.09 and 2.07) and triples the odds of postoperative decompensation (OR 3.04). Every estimate is crude and unadjusted, portal hypertension is a marker of more advanced cirrhosis, and the dramatic subgroup figures that justify measuring the hepatic venous pressure gradient come from three small studies totalling 115 patients, two of them the authors' own.
25212123.funding: Supported by Instituto de Salud Carlos III grants PI11/01830 to Bruix and FIS 13/00341 to Bosch, and by FEDER; CIBERehd is funded by the Instituto de Salud Carlos III. Bruix declares consultancy, advisory roles and grants from Bayer and relationships with BioCompatibles, Novartis, Daichi, Arqule, Abbott, Bristol-Myers Squibb, GlaxoSmithKline, Kowa, Lilly and Roche

limitations: Retrospective analysis, although the database was prospectively collected
The risk stratification was never externally validated, only internally cross-validated by 10-fold cross-validation
Surgical indications and tumour burden expanded over the 14-year study period
The authors acknowledge that definitions of postoperative decompensation vary widely between series, so their 19.9 percent rate is not comparable with others
The authors attribute the discrepancy between the random-forest variable ranking and the partitioning tree to the difference between the two methods
The authors predict the risk within each class will fall as hepatitis C is cured, so the absolute rates may overstate current risk
critique: The high-risk class contains 20 patients with 12 events, no confidence interval is given for its 60.0 percent decompensation rate or its 25.0 percent liver-related mortality (5 of 20), and 20 is exactly the minimum node size the tree was permitted to split at, so the class was created at the algorithm's own stopping boundary

The intermediate class holds 297 of 543 patients (54.7 percent) and merges three clinically unlike groups, no portal hypertension with a major resection, portal hypertension with a minor resection, and a minor resection with a MELD above 9, into a single 28.6 percent figure that cannot inform a decision about any of them

The cross-validated C index (0.78, 95% CI 0.74 to 0.82) exceeds the model's own apparent C index (0.76, 0.74 to 0.79), which is the wrong direction for cross-validation and indicates that the tree was re-grown within folds rather than the fixed tree being tested

The reported overall error rate of 0.06 is implausible for an outcome with 19.9 percent prevalence, since predicting no decompensation in everyone would err in about 20 percent of cases, and no confusion matrix appears in the main text

The odds ratios attached to the tree's splits are numerically identical to the univariable logistic odds ratios (portal hypertension 2.99, 1.93 to 4.62; major hepatectomy 2.98, 1.97 to 4.52 and 2.76, 1.85 to 4.77), so the hierarchy is presented with effect estimates that are not conditional on the splits they label

The random-forest importance measure ranks extent of hepatectomy above portal hypertension, reversing the order of the tree on which the paper's conclusion and title rest; the disagreement is instability in the ranking rather than a property of the two methods

The endpoint is a composite the authors defined in their own earlier work and is dominated by ascites: 101 of 108 events were Dindo-Clavien grade 2, 85 of those involved ascites, and 33 of the ascites cases drained less than 500 mL a day, so a large part of liver decompensation here is a mild drain output and a decision about when to remove a drain

Seventy-three patients with grade 1 liver-related complications were excluded from the endpoint as clinically irrelevant by the operating team, and moving that line turns a 19.9 percent rate into 33.3 percent

Portal hypertension, the tree's first and most important variable, was defined clinically by F1 varices or platelets below 100,000 with a spleen above 120 mm; no patient had a hepatic venous pressure gradient measured, so the model's top predictor is the surrogate definition that the guidelines it informs regard as insufficient

The MELD cut-point of 9 was selected by the tree's own maximisation in a cohort with a median MELD of 8 and an interquartile range of 7 to 10, so the third split divides the middle of the distribution at a data-driven threshold reported without any penalty for having searched for it

The extent of hepatectomy is a planned-operation variable chosen by surgeons who already knew the patient's portal hypertension status, so the second node partly encodes the team's own risk avoidance: only 20 of the 105 major resections were done in patients with portal hypertension, and those 20 are the high-risk class

Liver-related mortality by risk class (4.4, 9.0 and 25.0 percent) is cumulative over a median 66 months of follow-up and explicitly covers death at any time after surgery, yet it is presented alongside length of stay as though both described the perioperative period; 30-day mortality was zero and in-hospital mortality 0.9 percent

The cohort was deliberately operated beyond guidelines, with 24.9 percent outside Milan criteria, 22.7 percent multifocal, 11.8 percent BCLC B and 4.1 percent BCLC C, and 22.1 percent previously treated, by the same multidisciplinary board that four of the six authors sit on; no measure of tumour burden enters the model at any level

Liver-related mortality in the intermediate class is 27 of 297 (9.0 percent) in the text and 29 in Figure 2, final follow-up is 31 January 2015 in the abstract and 1 January 2015 in the Follow-up section, and the abstract quotes only the cross-validated C index while the Results give a lower apparent value

Fourteen years of single-centre practice are pooled with no year-of-surgery term in any model, across a period in which the unit's own technique changed (ultrasonic dissection, irrigated bipolar coagulation, central venous pressure below 5 mmHg, Pringle manoeuvre only on demand, intermittent clamping in 6.3 percent)
27248425.n: 543 patients with chronic liver disease who underwent curative resection for HCC at the National Cancer Institute of Milan between 1 January 2000 and 31 December 2013; 108 (19.9 percent) developed postoperative liver decompensation and 5 (0.9 percent) died in hospital
27248425.bottom_line: Builds a three-variable decision tree from 543 consecutive resections in which clinical portal hypertension, then extent of hepatectomy, then a MELD above 9 stratify postoperative liver decompensation into 4.9, 28.6 and 60.0 percent. The tree is internally cross-validated only, its high-risk class holds 20 patients, more than half the cohort lands in a single undifferentiated intermediate class, and the endpoint is dominated by grade 2 ascites, so it ranks risk rather than guiding an operation.
27248425.funding: Institutional; no funding source or conflict of interest is reported in the article

limitations: Imaging and survival were censored at transplantation, which the authors defend as the correct method for time to progression while acknowledging it as a limitation
Time to progression was used as a surrogate because survival in this population is confounded by crossover to other therapies
The study was halted on the recommendation of the cancer centre because of accrual difficulties
Only 45 of 179 eligible patients were randomised, with 43 declining research and others selecting a specific therapy
The authors state that the Child-Pugh B case mix explains survival lower than expected
critique: The hazard ratio of 0.122 rests on 12 progression events in 45 patients and its confidence interval spans roughly a twentyfold range, so the effect size is not estimable to any useful precision even though the direction is clear

The trial was stopped at 45 of 124 planned patients with no prespecified interim analysis, and the conditional power of 96.8 percent offered in mitigation is a hypothetical calculation assuming the protocol hazard ratio would have held in the 79 patients never enrolled

The arms were unbalanced on precisely the variables that determine progression and survival: half the Y-90 arm was Child-Pugh B at randomisation and 54 percent by the day of first treatment against 24 percent for chemoembolisation, with portal hypertension in 83 against 52 percent (p = 0.051), and no adjustment is made

Survival was identical between arms, so the trial demonstrates better local control rather than patient benefit, and the reduction in waiting-list dropout that the paper advances as the clinical rationale was never itself measured

Censoring at transplantation removes the most favourable outcomes from both arms, and with most patients listed for transplantation the proportion censored is large, which is why competing-risk and inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted analyses were needed to support the primary result

Enrolment was 25 percent of eligible patients at a single centre, with 49 requesting Y-90 and 13 requesting chemoembolisation outside the trial, so the randomised cohort is the minority indifferent between the two at a centre with a strong radioembolisation programme
Two of 21 chemoembolisation patients were treated off study, so the control arm as delivered is smaller still

Y-90 patients waited longer for their first treatment than chemoembolisation patients, which the authors present as a strength but which also means the two arms differ in the interval between staging and treatment

Three authors including the senior author advise the manufacturer of the device tested, and the trial's conclusion prompted the centre to change its own practice to radioembolisation for transplant bridging
The paper is universally cited as PREMIERE although it never uses that name, which makes its small size and single-centre origin easy to overlook
27575820.n: 45 of 179 eligible BCLC A or B patients with HCC not amenable to resection or ablation, randomised 1:1 at a single US centre between October 2009 and October 2015 to Y-90 glass microspheres at 120 Gy (24) or conventional chemoembolisation (21); most were listed for transplantation, and half the Y-90 arm was Child-Pugh B at randomisation
27575820.bottom_line: Widely cited as PREMIERE, this is a 45-patient single-centre randomised trial in which radioembolisation gave a much longer time to progression than chemoembolisation (median over 26 against 6.8 months, HR 0.122) with identical survival. It was stopped for slow accrual at a third of its planned size with no prespecified interim analysis, the endpoint is a surrogate censored at transplantation, and the arms were poorly balanced on liver function.
27575820.funding: Funded in part by NIH grant CA126809; three authors, including the senior author, advise BTG International, which manufactures the TheraSphere device tested

limitations: The trial enrolled only patients who progressed during sorafenib treatment, so the authors state that no firm conclusion can be drawn about regorafenib in patients who do not tolerate sorafenib
Special populations such as patients co-infected with HIV were not included

The authors note that the association between adverse events such as hand-foot skin reaction and outcome is based on post-randomisation events and so cannot be used to select patients likely to benefit
critique: Eligibility required documented tolerance of sorafenib before progression on it, which selects for tolerance of a related multikinase inhibitor as well, so the 10.6-month median and the manageable toxicity profile describe a population pre-selected on the exposure being tested

Every treated patient had an adverse event and 47 of 379 regorafenib patients discontinued for an adverse event unrelated to disease progression against 12 of 194 on placebo, so the 2.8-month median gain is bought at a cost the trial measured but discounted

Response and progression were assessed by investigators using mRECIST and RECIST with no blinded independent central review, and the two complete responses reported by mRECIST are a criterion that excludes necrosis of the target lesion from the measurement

Patients who progressed from Child-Pugh A to B between screening and randomisation were enrolled, disclosed only in a footnote to the baseline table, and 5 regorafenib and 6 placebo patients were Child-Pugh B at baseline
Asian recruitment was capped at 40 percent by design, which constrains the trial's representativeness of the global disease by administrative fiat rather than by eligibility

Pharmacokinetic and biomarker evaluations are stated not to be reported here, so the trial that established sorafenib-to-regorafenib sequencing published no biomarker that would identify who should receive it

238 of 843 screened patients failed screening, so roughly a third of patients considered for a trial restricted to sorafenib-tolerant progressors were still not eligible, and the paper gives no characteristics for them

All statistical analyses were performed by the funder, which also provided the drug, co-designed the trial, collected and interpreted the data, prepared the report and paid for the writing assistance, so no analysis independent of Bayer underlies the registration result
27932229.n: 573 of 843 screened patients with HCC, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0 or 1 who had tolerated sorafenib and progressed on it, randomised 2:1 to regorafenib (379) or placebo (194) between May 2013 and December 2015, with Asian recruitment capped at 40 percent; median prior sorafenib duration 7.8 months in both arms
27932229.bottom_line: RESORCE was the first trial to show a survival benefit for any systemic agent after sorafenib, with median overall survival 10.6 against 7.8 months (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.79) and gains in progression-free survival, time to progression and response. 27932229.funding: Funded by Bayer, which provided the study drug, designed the trial with the principal investigator and steering committee, took part in data collection and interpretation and in preparing the report, performed all statistical analyses and funded writing assistance; three authors are Bayer employees, one holding stock, and the principal investigator reports grants and personal fees from Bayer

limitations: More patients assigned radioembolisation than sorafenib never received their allocated treatment, which the authors state
There was a long work-up delay before radioembolisation

Dose-related efficacy had not been evaluated at the time of the report, which the authors list as a limitation
critique: Fifty-three of 237 patients assigned radioembolisation never received it and about half of those crossed to sorafenib, so the intention-to-treat hazard ratio of 1.15 becomes 0.99 with identical 9.9-month medians in the per-protocol set; the trial cannot distinguish an ineffective treatment from an undelivered one
